He also knows that he feels hopeful about this approach and that he intends to fully commit to it. He knows Teresa verbally agrees that things feel less overwhelming and that she accepts the plan. He also does not know for certain that the collaboration will objectively work; he only believes and hopes it will.

From Arthur’s perspective, his intention to commit to the collaborative approach leads directly to his concrete action: he proposes a division of tasks, says he will handle inventory, and commits to checking in regularly. Thus, the intention influences his action by making him actively engage in the collaborative tasks.
